expected_causal_sequence.description: Battery cell 3 begins to drift out of balance; this is the earliest observable precursor, five minutes before the injected fault window opens.
The injected power_degradation fault begins on battery cell 3, raising internal resistance and reducing terminal voltage under load.
Battery terminal voltage crosses the 26.2 V warning threshold as the degraded cell carries the bus load.
EPS sheds 85 W of non-essential load to protect the main bus.
Battery heater power is cut from 18 W to 8 W as part of load shedding.
Available power falls below the mission allocation, reducing the operating envelope for every downstream subsystem.
Reduced heater and pump power let the thermal loop drift above its setpoint.
Reaction-wheel torque authority is reduced and attitude error exceeds 0.5 deg.
Transmitter power is reduced from 10.5 W to 7.4 W to preserve the bus.
The flight computer spends more time on power and mode management, and CPU load exceeds 75%.
A marginal bus triggers a watchdog reset, interrupting attitude and communications control.
The onboard computer enters safe mode and sheds payload and non-essential loads.
Downlink rate falls to 64 kbps and signal-to-noise ratio approaches the critical threshold.
Battery terminal voltage crosses the 24.8 V critical threshold.
Battery temperature crosses 32 degC while thermal control remains degraded.
Mission operations declare a mission-level failure because payload downlink cannot be recovered in safe mode.
Safe mode stabilizes at a reduced power state, with the battery above the 20% state-of-charge critical limit.

notes: Evaluation-only data for the synthetic battery-failure demo. The injected fault is a 0.22-magnitude power degradation on battery cell 3 in the electrical power system, starting at MET 900 s (2026-03-14T08:15:00Z) and lasting 2100 s. The causal sequence is the graded expectation for root-cause and propagation analysis; never include this file in hypothesis-agent inputs.
